angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,987 km at 48.88 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 20.4576 +/- 0.0123 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 48.88 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.631 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Peláez-Torres et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2274 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract): 438,987 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.612 +/- 0.0202 solar masses from Peláez-Torres et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2274 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3943 +/- 157 K from Peláez-Torres et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2274 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Peláez-Torres et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2274 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2274.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.625, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
